comment: Defects of the game's own data that the engine reports correctly and cannot fix (we never ship or patch game data files). A scene whose only problems match an entry here is reported as KNOWN, not as failed; anything else still fails it. Each entry: the game version, the scene (or "*": any scene, for a defect of the game's timed scripts that shows wherever the sweep happens to be), the game file at fault, the exact text the sweep sees (a substring of the reason), and why it cannot be fixed. Remove an entry once its cause is gone.

defects.error: engine error: geometry: resource\models\locations\UnderWater\UnderWater.gm has 86193 vertices but its vertex colour file resource\models\locations\UnderWater\UnderWater_morning10.col has 83897 entries
defects.reason: The game ships a baked vertex colour file made for an older version of the model (2296 vertices fewer). The engine reports it (geom_static.cpp) and draws the model's own vertex colours, as the original engine did; the data is the game's.

defects.error: missing texture: Can't load texture resource\textures\PHONG256_BW.GIF.tx
defects.reason: The sloop of the main menu (sloop1_mast2.gm, also sloop1_mast201.gm and Frigate_h1.gm) names the texture PHONG256_BW.GIF, which the game does not ship (not in RESOURCE/Textures of the installer). The engine logs it and draws the mast without that texture, as the original engine does; the data is the game's.

The game's script that moves the free captains (PsHero) between towns when a day passes picks a destination t<rand(iNum-1)>; when the captain's town has no travel paths iNum is 0, the script itself traces "Can't find travel path", falls back to t0 and reads arDest.t0.town, which does not exist: missed attribute t0, null ap, no rAP data, all at line 924. It is the game's own script on the state of a new game with days passing (the sweep passes a day between locations); it fires on the day change, whatever scene is loading, and the scene still renders. Seen once so far, at loc:Plantation_F1 at midnight; not checked whether a played game reaches the same state.
